channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Manufacturing
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Attackers are abusing a Siemens Software Center flaw in ClickFix malware campaigns, and CISA has added it to KEV with a 3 November deadline
item.category: Top Story
item.description: Siemens confirmed on 19 October that CVE-2026-110936, a DLL search-path flaw in Siemens Software Center, its tool for downloading, installing and activating purchased software, is being exploited in what it calls the Romulus multi-platform ClickFix campaign. Attackers ship a genuine, validly signed copy of the program with their own DLLs in an installer; when a user is talked into running it, the program loads the attackers’ code, even on PCs that never had Software Center. Siemens says no Siemens system, product or update channel was breached, and it names no malware family. The flaw is rated CVSS v3.1 6.7 (v4.0 8.4); V4.0.9.8 fixes it, and existing installs update on next start. CISA added it to KEV on 20 October with a 3 November deadline and republished the advisory on 22 October, listing critical manufacturing among affected sectors. No targets are named, but a trusted Siemens signature makes such a lure more convincing to plant engineers (editorial assessment). - Siemens ProductCERT SSA-580366, 15 Oct 2026, updated 17 and 19 Oct, and exploitation notice, 19 Oct 2026 (primary); CISA KEV, 20 Oct 2026; CISA ICSA-26-295-03, 22 Oct 2026; SecurityWeek, 19 Oct 2026 - Exploitation confirmed 19 Oct 2026; KEV due 3 Nov 2026; fix V4.0.9.8

item.title: [High] Microsoft ties the ConnectWise Cloud Backup compromise to China-aligned Storm-0940 and lists manufacturing, automotive, chemicals and semiconductors among its targets
item.category: Supply-chain compromise — ConnectWise Cloud Backup app identities used against Microsoft 365 tenants; Microsoft names manufacturing, automotive, chemicals and semiconductor among targeted sectors
item.description: Microsoft said on 21 October that it assesses Storm-0940, which it calls a China-state aligned actor active since 2021, was responsible for the recently disclosed ConnectWise supply-chain compromise. The attackers controlled the identities of several ConnectWise cloud applications tied to Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) and used them to sign in to customers’ Microsoft 365 tenants as the application, so MFA did not apply; a separate password spray on 10–14 October did not succeed. Microsoft says attempts reached more than 2,250 tenants, that most of the targeting failed, and that in several cases privileged access followed in under three hours. It says the actor used ARTEX, an open-source penetration-testing framework that can drive any AI model, and lists aerospace and defense, automotive, chemicals, energy, manufacturing and semiconductors among targeted sectors. ConnectWise suspended Cloud Backup, SaaS Security and Cloud Management, is restoring them in phases, and says it has no evidence that partner backup data was compromised. Victim counts reported by others differ; Huntress reported unauthorized sign-ins at 162 tenants it monitors. No manufacturing victim or OT impact has been named. Manufacturers whose MSP manages Microsoft 365 through these services should check their tenants (editorial assessment). - Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 21 Oct 2026 (primary); ConnectWise statements via CyberScoop and Cybersecurity Dive, 17–21 Oct 2026; Huntress via BleepingComputer - Attribution published 21 Oct 2026; ConnectWise restoring services in phases

item.title: [High] FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed credential theft against FortiGate gateways is still running, with targets in all 16 critical-infrastructure sectors
item.category: Campaign — FortiGate firewall and SSL VPN credential theft; no CVE; access feeds ransomware
item.description: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on 6 October, in joint advisory JCSA-20261006-01, that the FortiBleed campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPNs remains an active threat. There is no CVE: the agencies describe abuse of reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage, and researchers describe password spraying and stuffing, offline cracking of extracted hashes and a sniffer that captures authentication traffic. Attackers have added admin accounts and deleted or reset legitimate ones, locking owners out. The agencies say targets span all 16 US critical-infrastructure sectors, critical manufacturing among them, and the FBI ties the access to Payload ransomware; SOCRadar, which reports overlaps with INC and Lynx, says it has confirmed at least 12 ransomware deployments from this access and counted 86,644 working device credentials across 194 countries as of 19 June. No OT system compromise has been described. FortiGate often sits at the IT/OT boundary in plants, so a stolen admin login there is a path toward production networks (editorial assessment). - FBI/US Secret Service joint advisory JCSA-20261006-01, 6 Oct 2026 (primary); Cybersecurity Dive and The Hacker News, 7 Oct 2026 - Warning issued 6 Oct 2026; the 86,644 credential count dates from 19 Jun 2026

item.title: [High] Microsoft: a ransomware affiliate rotating Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT lists critical manufacturing among 14 targeted sectors
item.category: Ransomware — Multi-brand affiliate tradecraft, initial access unconfirmed
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published a profile on 24 September of Storm-2570, a ransomware affiliate that deploys Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis or BERT while its hands-on tradecraft stays the same. Microsoft lists 14 affected sectors, including critical manufacturing, chemicals, energy, and food and agriculture, and names no victims. It says how the group gets in remains unconfirmed. Once inside, the affiliate relies on remote-management tools (Atera, MeshAgent, ScreenConnect, Splashtop), scanning and PsExec, credential theft with Mimikatz, LaZagne and ntdsutil, Rclone or s5cmd to move data out, and Cloudflared or ngrok for tunnelling. Black Kite’s count through July puts Qilin first and DragonForce fourth among ransomware groups hitting manufacturers, so this playbook overlaps with the most active brands against the sector. - Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 24 Sep 2026 (primary) - Profile published 24 Sep 2026; initial access unconfirmed

item.title: [Medium] Symantec: Russia’s APT28 spent at least two months inside a NATO naval shipbuilder’s network and also hit a military aircraft-engine maker
item.category: Espionage — APT28 (Symantec: Swallowtail) inside a NATO naval shipbuilder and a military aircraft-engine maker; IT only, no OT impact reported
item.description: Symantec reported on 20 October that Swallowtail, which it equates with APT28 (Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard; the US government considers it a GRU unit), broke into a naval shipbuilder and a manufacturer of military aircraft engines, as well as a law-enforcement agency, in two unnamed NATO member states. At the shipbuilder, a macro-laden Word attachment opened on 24 July dropped the Hookedge backdoor; within days the operators set up a persistent SSH tunnel, ran a PowerShell script to capture NTLM credentials and mapped internal DNS and privileges, and on 31 July deployed a previously undocumented loader whose payload was not recovered. The launcher was last seen on 24 September. Symantec reports IT-network reconnaissance and credential capture only: no OT, ICS or production impact and no confirmed data theft, and it names no victim. It has published indicators, which defence and aerospace suppliers should check against their own networks (editorial assessment). - Symantec Threat Hunter Team, 20 Oct 2026 (primary); Cybersecurity Dive, 21 Oct 2026; CyberScoop, 20 Oct 2026 - Intrusion from 24 Jul 2026, last seen 24 Sep 2026; IT espionage, no OT impact reported

item.title: [Medium] Attackers took over refrigeration controllers in about 700 French supermarkets; plants run similar web-managed controllers
item.category: Cross-sector lesson — confirmed OT attack on French supermarket refrigeration controllers (food retail, not manufacturing)
item.description: Over the nights of 11–13 October, attackers remotely changed settings on web-managed refrigeration controllers in French supermarkets, stretching defrost cycles so that some cabinets reached about 50°C, spoiling stock and, according to the Paris prosecutor, starting fires at some stores. Finance Minister Roland Lescure put the toll at about 700 stores on 13 October, across Carrefour, Coopérative U, E.Leclerc, Intermarché/Netto and Monoprix. CERT-FR’s alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 named Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers on 12 October, added Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb on 13 October, and on 16 October said attack campaigns are probably still ongoing; it has not been revised since, and no new attack nights have been reported after 13 October. Danfoss says most affected units are end-of-life or on outdated firmware, and Copeland points to a discontinued, end-of-life generation. No group has claimed it, no ransom was demanded and the entry route is not established. On 22 October Forescout counted 12,976 internet-exposed refrigeration-management service observations on 6,017 IP addresses in 99 countries, found about 80% of observed Danfoss AK-SM 800A StoreView services on firmware older than 4.3.1, and named food processing among the sectors at risk. This is a food-retail incident, not a manufacturing one; we carry it because plants run cold rooms, chillers and building systems from similar web-managed controllers, and any that are reachable from the internet face the same risk (editorial assessment). - CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012, 12 Oct 2026, updated 13 and 16 Oct 2026 (primary); AP, 13 Oct 2026; SecurityWeek, 15 Oct 2026; Forescout Vedere Labs, 22 Oct 2026 - Attacks 11–13 Oct 2026; CERT-FR says campaigns are probably still ongoing (16 Oct 2026); no new attack nights reported since

item.title: [High] US, UK and German agencies warn that SafePay ransomware has hit at least 600 organizations since August 2024, getting in through stolen credentials and old edge-device flaws
item.category: Advisory — #StopRansomware: SafePay (AA26-293A), cross-sector; no sectors or victims named
item.description: CISA, the FBI and the US Secret Service, with Germany’s LKA Rheinland-Pfalz, the UK National Crime Agency and the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit, issued advisory AA26-293A on 20 October about SafePay, a closed ransomware group with no affiliates. The agencies count at least 600 victim organizations across multiple critical-infrastructure sectors in the Americas, Europe and Australia since August 2024. SafePay gets in with exposed or brute-forced credentials, phished accounts and VPN logins, often from Mullvad addresses, and by exploiting older edge-device flaws, including CVE-2020-3259 and CVE-2023-20269. Once inside it uses WinRM, PsExec and RDP, takes data with tools such as RClone and WinSCP, deletes shadow copies and resets NAS devices that hold backups, then encrypts and threatens to leak. As reported, the advisory names no sectors or victims. We carry it because industrial firms made up 31% of the ransomware victims NCC Group counted in August, and SafePay’s entry points are the VPNs and remote-access gear that front many plants (editorial assessment). - CISA/FBI/USSS joint advisory AA26-293A, 20 Oct 2026, as reported by BleepingComputer and Cybersecurity Dive, 21 Oct 2026 - At least 600 victims since Aug 2024; activity observed Nov 2024 to Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Ransomware claims hit a 2026 high in August, with industrial firms 31% of victims, and a new group, Aurora, is exploiting VPNs
item.category: Report — Ransomware landscape, industrial sector
item.description: NCC Group’s August review, published 23 September, counts 1,073 ransomware attacks, up 12% from July’s 960 and the highest month of 2026, with industrials (a broader class than manufacturing alone) taking 329, or 31%, up from 28% in July. Qilin led with 15% of attacks, overtaking The Gentlemen, and North America took 44% of the total. NCC also profiles Aurora, a ransomware-as-a-service group active since late April that exploits VPNs against manufacturing, legal, research and transportation targets; in one August transportation case NCC’s responders saw it encrypt hypervisors while also extorting for stolen data. Black Kite’s 18 September report points the same way: 1,183 manufacturing victims through July, up 39.7% year over year, with Qilin (178), The Gentlemen (142), Akira (96), DragonForce (70) and INC Ransom (65) leading. NCC’s counts are based on leak-site postings, so they measure claimed attacks, not confirmed plant downtime. - NCC Group monthly threat review, 23 Sep 2026 (primary); Industrial Cyber, 28 Sep 2026; Black Kite report, 18 Sep 2026 - August 2026 data; Black Kite data through Jul 2026

item.title: [Medium] In lab tests, an AI model found and moved a robotic arm within minutes, and an AI coding agent rebuilt a published controller exploit for about $6
item.category: Research — AI agents against OT: Booz Allen lab tests and Claroty Team82 exploit reproduction; no new CVE
item.description: Booz Allen’s 8 October report describes frontier AI models tested in its isolated, multi-vendor OT lab, which is modelled on a manufacturing facility. Across eight scenarios the models met every test objective; in one they went from a perimeter compromise to actions inside the industrial control network in just over 16 minutes, with a human approving every exploit and any action with a physical effect. One model identified a robotic arm, mapped its protection zones and motion limits and moved it within minutes; in another test the models found live, pre-authenticated connections to 14 OT devices. Some controls held: a controller rejected a stop command and a motor in local-control mode refused remote starts. A Booz Allen researcher told Dark Reading that removing the approval step would roughly halve the time, and Industrial Cyber reports that the company calls the findings preliminary. Separately, Claroty’s Team82 reported on 13 October that an AI coding agent, redirected by a researcher and connected to the Ghidra reverse-engineering tool, reproduced three previously disclosed Danfoss AK-SM 800A flaws and chained them to root on a lab device in about 28 minutes for roughly $6 of usage, working from publicly downloadable firmware. Team82 stresses this was not autonomous discovery and does not link the flaws to the French supermarket attacks. Both are lab results, not real-world attacks. - Booz Allen report, 8 Oct 2026 (primary), covered by SecurityWeek (14 Oct), Dark Reading (16 Oct) and Industrial Cyber (20 Oct 2026); Claroty Team82, 13 Oct 2026 (primary) - Published 8 and 13 Oct 2026; lab results only

item.title: [Low] Nozomi’s summer telemetry puts manufacturing first for OT/IoT alerts per organization, with credential techniques about a third of detections
item.category: Report — Nozomi Networks Labs OT/IoT telemetry, June–August 2026
item.description: Nozomi Networks Labs’ review of June–August 2026 customer telemetry, published 12 October, ranks manufacturing first for alerts per organization, ahead of transportation and of energy, utilities and waste, which moved up to third. Credential-related techniques made up roughly a third of detections. Among alerts Nozomi attributed to named actors, Scattered Spider accounted for close to half, and Russia-linked or Russian-speaking actors together for more than a third. Siemens PLCs and Rockwell products were among the vulnerable products detected most often, and Nozomi says 58% of 2026 vulnerabilities rate High or Critical, against 48% in 2025. Alerts per organization measures what sensors flag in customer networks, not confirmed intrusions. - Nozomi Networks Labs, 12 Oct 2026 (primary) - Telemetry period Jun–Aug 2026

item.title: [Critical] Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain gave attackers root on fully patched VPNs, and one link is still unpatched
item.category: Exploited edge appliance — Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain; CVE-2026-104935 in CISA KEV; third flaw without a public fix
item.description: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that a chain of three flaws was used against a limited number of Connect Secure customers to run commands as root on fully patched appliances. Two of the flaws are fixed under one CVE, CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS v3.1 8.6), which CISA added to KEV the same day with a 16 October deadline; the third, a privilege escalation, has no CVE and no patch yet. Volexity found the chain while handling a customer incident and tracks the attacker as UTA0576, a new cluster; exploitation dates to at least early October (1–3 October). The intruders stole domain credentials, searched Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys, sprayed passwords and wiped logs, leaving no web shell. CISA and Volexity warn that Ivanti’s Integrity Checker may miss the compromise. Volexity said on 13 October that the third flaw would be patched “in the coming weeks”; no public CVE or patch for it had been reported by 23 October. No manufacturer has been named, but Connect Secure often carries engineer and integrator remote access into plant networks (editorial assessment). - Ivanti security advisory and Volexity research, 13 Oct 2026 (primary); CISA KEV, 13 Oct 2026; CyberScoop, SecurityWeek and Cybersecurity Dive, 13–14 Oct 2026 - Exploited since at least 1–3 Oct 2026; KEV due 16 Oct 2026; no public fix for the third flaw found as of 23 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Citrix patches a fourth critical NetScaler flaw, CVE-2026-107406, while the campaign behind three exploited zero-days continues
item.category: Exploited edge appliance — Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway: three KEV-listed zero-days plus a fourth critical SAML flaw (CVE-2026-107406)
item.description: Citrix published bulletin CTX697191 on 8 October for CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS v4.0 9.5), a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway set up as a SAML service provider or identity provider that Citrix says may lead to code execution or denial of service. It is not reported exploited and is not in KEV as of CISA’s 21 October catalog, but the builds that fixed the September zero-days (14.1-73.37 to 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.23 to 13.1-64.28) stay vulnerable when used as a SAML identity provider, so those appliances need another upgrade. The campaign itself runs on the three earlier flaws: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (KEV 27 September) and CVE-2026-88779 (KEV 4 October), which Citrix and watchTowr describe as a denial-of-service bug; CISA says attackers use it to force reboots so that code planted through CVE-2026-88771 runs. Mandiant counts dozens of victim organizations and describes suspected state-nexus actors without naming a group; Arctic Wolf counts at least 78 targeted organizations, and Shadowserver sees more than 20,000 exposed instances. No manufacturer has been named. NetScaler Gateway commonly fronts contractor and remote-engineer access into plant DMZs (editorial assessment). - Citrix bulletins CTX697191 (8 Oct 2026) and CTX697174 (primary); CISA KEV catalog 2026.10.21; Cybersecurity Dive, 12 Oct 2026; The Hacker News, 9 Oct 2026 - Fourth flaw disclosed 8 Oct 2026, not in KEV; earlier three KEV-listed 27 Sep and 4 Oct 2026; more than 20,000 instances exposed per Shadowserver

item.title: [Critical] Cisco SD-WAN Manager authentication bypass and a FortiMail file-write zero-day are both exploited and KEV-listed, each at CVSS 9.8
item.category: Exploited edge flaws — Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager and Fortinet FortiMail, both in CISA KEV
item.description: Cisco disclosed on 30 September that CVE-2026-76504 in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, an improper handling of URI encoding, lets an unauthenticated remote attacker bypass an authentication rule on an API endpoint and gain administrator-level access. Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in September, scores the flaw CVSS 9.8, lists no workarounds and fixes it in 20.9.10.1, 20.12.8.2, 20.15.6.1, 20.18.4.1, 26.1.2.1 and 26.2.1; releases older than 20.9 must migrate. It revised the advisory on 2 October, and CISA added the flaw to KEV on 30 September with a 3 October deadline. BleepingComputer counts it as the fifth exploited SD-WAN zero-day of 2026. Separately, Fortinet’s FG-IR-26-175 (1 October) covers CVE-2026-104286 in FortiMail, a path traversal that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files through crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests (CVSS 9.8). Fortinet says it has been reported as exploited in the wild, and CISA listed it in KEV the same day with a 4 October deadline. Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2, with 7.2 users told to move to 7.4 or later. Neither vendor names an actor or victims. For multi-site manufacturers, SD-WAN Manager is the controller that configures links between plants, warehouses and head office, so admin access there reaches every site at once (editorial assessment). - Cisco advisory cisco-sa-sdwan-webauth-xr8beuuU, 30 Sep 2026, revised 2 Oct (primary); Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-175, 1 Oct 2026, updated 5 Oct (primary); CISA KEV; BleepingComputer - KEV-listed 30 Sep and 1 Oct 2026; Fortinet fixed releases listed 5 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] Siemens: critical web-server flaws in S7-1500 and ET 200SP CPUs have no fix yet, alongside TM MFP and Industrial Edge advisories
item.category: Vendor advisories — Siemens ProductCERT October release: S7-1500 / ET 200SP CPU web server, S7-1500 TM MFP, Industrial Edge
item.description: Siemens’ 13 October release (17 advisories by SecurityWeek’s count) includes SSA-591731: eight web-server flaws, CVE-2026-63350 to CVE-2026-63357, across all versions of S7-1500, ET 200SP, ET 200pro and Drive Controller CPUs, rated CVSS v3.1 9.6 (v4.0 9.4). An attacker could run code in an authorized user’s browser and carry out PLC operations with that user’s rights; there is no fix yet, only mitigations. SSA-784472 lists 377 CVEs, the highest rated CVSS v3.1 10.0, in the optional GNU/Linux subsystem of the S7-1500 TM MFP technology module, also without a fix. SSA-832641 covers authenticated path traversal in Industrial Edge devices (CVE-2026-44415, CVSS v3.1 9.1) that can expose or delete data; fixes are out for Industrial Edge devices, IoT2050 and several SIMATIC IPCs, but not yet for SCALANCE LPE9413/9433 or the affected HMI panels. None of these Siemens flaws is reported exploited or listed in KEV (the exploited Software Center flaw in the top story is separate). CISA republished the October advisories on 22 October as ICSA-26-295-02 to -18, and its versions still show no fix for the S7 PLC web server, the GNU/Linux subsystems of the S7-1500 TM MFP and CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP, or WinCC V7.5 (CVE-2026-59241, CVSS v3.1 8.8; WinCC V8.0 Update 11 and V8.1 Update 7 are fixed). The S7-1500 is one of the most widely used PLC families on production lines, so its web server is the item to check first (editorial assessment). - Siemens ProductCERT SSA-591731, SSA-784472 and SSA-832641, 13 Oct 2026 (primary); CISA republications ICSA-26-295-02 to -18, 22 Oct 2026; SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday roundup, 14 Oct 2026 - Published 13 Oct 2026; republished by CISA 22 Oct 2026; S7 web-server, TM MFP and WinCC V7.5 fixes pending

item.title: [Critical] Nozomi finds 19 flaws in a Pepperl+Fuchs IO-Link master, including a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass that chains to root
item.category: Vulnerability — Pepperl+Fuchs IO-Link masters, CVSS 9.8, fixed in firmware 1.7.8
item.description: Nozomi Networks Labs published research on 24 September describing 19 vulnerabilities in the web management interface of the Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2-8IOL-K45P-RJ45 IO-Link master (EtherNet/IP firmware 1.7.3). The worst, CVE-2026-27546 (CVSS 9.8), lets any network-reachable attacker obtain an admin session without credentials; chained with OS command injection flaws that run as root, it gives full control of the device. CERT@VDE’s coordinated advisory VDE-2026-014 (16 September) covers 22 CVEs across nine ICE2 and ICE3 models on firmware below 1.7.4, including a second CVSS 9.8 flaw (CVE-2026-27565) in which a malicious IODD file upload runs shell scripts as root, and tells users to install firmware 1.7.8. No exploitation is reported. IO-Link masters bridge sensors and actuators on a machine to the plant’s EtherNet/IP network, so a compromised master is a foothold inside the cell. - Nozomi Networks Labs, 24 Sep 2026 (primary); CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-014, 16 Sep 2026 (primary) - Published 16–24 Sep 2026; fix: firmware 1.7.8

item.title: [High] BeyondTrust Remote Support and a FortiOS flaw join KEV, and Unit 42 says Qilin and INC use a GlobalProtect bug to get VPN sessions past MFA
item.category: Exploited remote-access and firewall flaws — BeyondTrust Remote Support, Fortinet FortiOS, Palo Alto PAN-OS and GlobalProtect, SonicWall SMA1000
item.description: CISA added BeyondTrust Remote Support CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS v4.0 9.3) to KEV on 16 October with a 19 October deadline. Google’s Threat Intelligence Group says the suspected PRC-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221) exploited it as a zero-day from late August to gain root, harvest credentials and delete logs; BeyondTrust shipped patch BT26-05-RS on 8 October, and self-hosted appliances without auto-update must be patched by hand. The same day CISA listed Fortinet CVE-2025-61624, an authenticated FortiOS CLI path traversal that Fortinet rates Medium and fixed in April. Unit 42 reported on 14 October that attackers who broke into a telecom managed-service provider through FortiManager (CVE-2024-47575) used it to gain root on managed FortiGates; configuration and credential material for more than 500 FortiGates was exposed, though Unit 42 does not confirm intrusion into those customer networks and names no state. The CVE record lists Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808, which runs FortiOS, as affected. On 19–20 October Unit 42 reported that Qilin and INC ransomware exploit GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257, patched in May, to open VPN sessions past MFA and then move to vCenter, ESXi and Veeam, with manufacturing among targeted sectors. PAN-OS CVE-2026-0322 has been in KEV since 14 October, and SonicWall SMA1000’s CVE-2026-102255 still draws only attempts. OEMs, MSPs and integrators often reach plant networks through tools like these (editorial assessment). - Google Threat Intelligence Group, 15 Oct 2026, and Unit 42, 14 Oct 2026 (primary); CISA KEV catalog 2026.10.21; Fortinet FG-IR-26-122; Unit 42 GlobalProtect update via The Hacker News, 20 Oct 2026; Palo Alto Networks advisory, 14 Oct 2026; SonicWall SNWLID-2026-0017, 6 Oct 2026 - KEV-listed 14 and 16 Oct 2026; deadlines of 17 and 19 Oct 2026 have passed

item.title: [High] PHP2Shell reaches OT software: Schneider Electric has no fix yet for EcoStruxure Control Engineering, and ABB and Moxa have issued notices
item.category: Third-party component flaw — PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 / -109619) in OT software: Schneider Electric, ABB and Moxa notices
item.description: Two PHP flaws known as PHP2Shell, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allow unauthenticated remote code execution on servers running PHP; the PHP team rates each CVSS v4.0 9.2 and fixed them on 21 October in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Amazon says exploitation attempts began on 17 October, four days before the patches, and attempts now number in the millions, but no successful compromise has been confirmed and the flaws are not in KEV as of CISA’s 21 October catalog. OT vendors are now checking their products. Schneider Electric’s SESB-2026-295-01 (22 October) lists EcoStruxure Security Expert, fixed in 1.48.4.0; ProLeiT LINEoptimize (formerly Plant iT LMS), with remediation through ProLeiT support; and EcoStruxure Control Engineering, all versions, for which Schneider is still establishing a remediation plan. ABB has listed an APROL notice (SA26P015) and Moxa has published a response (MPSA-260001); check both for your products. A further PHP flaw disclosed on 23 October, CVE-2026-115560, affects only unusual configurations and has no fix yet. Engineering and plant-management servers that bundle PHP should not be reachable from the internet or user networks (editorial assessment). - Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01, 22 Oct 2026 (primary); ABB and Moxa advisory listings, 22–23 Oct 2026; PHP releases, 21 Oct 2026; BleepingComputer, 22 Oct 2026; The Hacker News, 23 Oct 2026 - PHP fixed 21 Oct 2026; attempts since 17 Oct 2026; EcoStruxure Control Engineering fix pending

item.title: [High] CISA: a WAGO controller flaw lets a low-privileged user run commands as root, a Moxa edge gateway has a hard-coded key, and PCAN drivers can crash Windows
item.category: Advisories — CISA ICSA-26-293-02 (WAGO), ICSA-26-293-03 (Moxa AIG-302), ICSA-26-293-01 (HMS Networks PEAK-System PCAN drivers)
item.description: CISA’s 20 October batch republished WAGO’s CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-096 as ICSA-26-293-02. On CC100, PFC100 G2, PFC200 G2, TP600, Edge Controller and WP400 devices below firmware 4.10.0 (FW32), CVE-2026-80466 (CVSS v3.1 8.8) lets a low-privileged remote user inject operating-system commands through the routing settings of the web-based management, which a root helper script then runs; CVE-2026-88850 (v3.1 8.1) lets low-privileged users change root-owned PROFIBUS parameters. The fix is firmware 4.10.0 (FW32), the release that also fixes the CODESYS issues WAGO disclosed on 1 October. ICSA-26-293-03 covers the Moxa AIG-302 edge gateway with ThingsPro Edge 1.4.0 and earlier: CVE-2026-109813 is a hard-coded cryptographic key (v3.1 8.1, v4.0 8.6) and CVE-2026-109812 a missing-authorization flaw (v3.1 6.8, v4.0 6.9), both fixed in 1.4.1. ICSA-26-293-01 covers six local flaws in HMS Networks’ PEAK-System PCAN CAN-interface drivers for Windows (5.1.2 and earlier) that can crash the kernel, the highest CVE-2026-103672 at v3.1 7.1; CISA says they are not remotely exploitable, and 5.1.4 fixes them. CISA lists critical manufacturing among affected sectors for all three, and none is reported exploited. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-293-01, -02 and -03, 20 Oct 2026 (primary); CERT@VDE VDE-2026-096 (WAGO); Moxa MPSA-262560 - Published 20 Oct 2026; no known exploitation

item.title: [High] Mitsubishi Electric fixes an authentication bypass in ICONICS GENESIS SCADA software, but MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz will get no fix
item.category: Vendor advisory — Mitsubishi Electric 2026-006, ICONICS GENESIS64 / GENESIS SCADA and HMI suite; CVSS v4.0 up to 9.4
item.description: Mitsubishi Electric’s advisory 2026-006, published 15 October, covers flaws across the ICONICS GENESIS64 and GENESIS SCADA and HMI suite. CVE-2026-16436 (CVSS v4.0 9.2) is an authentication bypass: a shared, fixed challenge-response can unlock any user account, although a remote attacker must first obtain that response. CVE-2026-16438 (v4.0 9.4) concerns default DCOM permissions granted to the administrator account, CVE-2026-16437 (v4.0 7.1) lets an administrator read or write the challenge-response file, and the older libwebp flaw CVE-2023-4863 (v4.0 9.3) affects ICONICS Suite 10.97 to 10.97.2 if a local administrator imports a crafted file. Affected are GENESIS 11.03 and earlier; GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and IoTWorX 10.97.3 and earlier; and all versions of MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz. Fixes are ICONICS Suite and IoTWorX 10.98, GENESIS 11.04 and, for libwebp, ICONICS Suite 10.97.3; MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz will not be fixed. No exploitation is reported. GENESIS64 and Hyper Historian commonly run plant HMIs and historians (editorial assessment). - Mitsubishi Electric PSIRT advisory 2026-006, 15 Oct 2026 (primary) - Published 15 Oct 2026; not exploited; no CISA republication found in the 20 or 22 Oct batches

item.title: [High] Rockwell fixes an ArmorBlock I/O flaw that lets anyone reset its web password; Schneider and ABB flag HMI and account-takeover bugs
item.category: Vendor advisories — Rockwell 1732E ArmorBlock I/O (SD1801); Schneider Electric Pro-face/Harmony STW6 HMIs; ABB dynovaPRO
item.description: Rockwell’s only new October advisory, SD1801, covers 1732E ArmorBlock I/O modules on firmware 3.012 and earlier. CVE-2026-12655 (CVSS v3.1 9.1, v4.0 8.8) is a capture-replay authentication bypass that lets an unauthenticated attacker change the web-server password and take over the module’s admin account; CVE-2026-12656 (CVSS v3.1 7.5) is a network-storm denial of service that needs a power cycle to clear. Rockwell found both internally, fixes them in firmware 3.013 and lists no workaround. Schneider Electric’s SEVD-2026-286-01 (13 October) says an unmaintained third-party component in Pro-face STW6000 and Harmony STW6 HMIs (all versions; CVE-2026-96434, CVSS v3.1 8.8) could let an attacker take control of the panel if a user visits a malicious web page. SecurityWeek’s 14 October roundup adds that ABB’s dynovaPRO advisory covers the Keycloak password-reset bypass CVE-2026-18963 (CVSS 9.1, first published in August); ABB knows of no exploitation, but its logs show 26 password-change events across nine customers that may be testing. ArmorBlock modules sit on machines on the plant floor, so admin takeover lets an attacker change I/O configuration inside the cell (editorial assessment). - Rockwell Automation SD1801 and Schneider Electric SEVD-2026-286-01, 13 Oct 2026 (primary); SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday roundup, 14 Oct 2026 - Published 13 Oct 2026; ArmorBlock fix 3.013

item.title: [High] CISA: Red Lion N-Tron 700 switches keep factory admin logins active and accept unauthenticated SNMP changes; the fix is firmware 3.11.1
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-281-01, Red Lion N-Tron 700 Series managed industrial switches; seven CVEs; fix firmware 3.11.1
item.description: CISA’s ICSA-26-281-01 (8 October; Update A on 15 October revised the CVSS v4.0 scores) covers seven flaws in Red Lion (HMS Networks) N-Tron 700 Series industrial Ethernet switches, reported by Idaho National Laboratory. The factory default admin credentials stay active after other administrators are configured; SNMP can change configuration, accounts and firmware without authentication and can trigger a TFTP export of plaintext credentials; firmware and bootloader updates are neither signed nor authenticated; and a URL can reboot the switch. The authentication bypass requires physical access. The highest CVSS v3.1 score is 8.3, with v4.0 scores up to 9.3 in the CVE records. Firmware 3.11.0 and earlier and bootloader 2.0.6.1 and earlier are affected, and the fix is firmware 3.11.1 or later. CISA lists critical manufacturing among the affected sectors and knows of no public exploitation. A compromised switch can expose or reroute traffic between controllers and HMIs (editorial assessment). - CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-281-01, 8 Oct 2026, Update A 15 Oct 2026 (primary) - Published 8 Oct 2026; updated 15 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CISA flags an Ignition privilege-escalation flaw, six bugs in the Eclipse Milo OPC UA library and end-of-life EasyIO controllers that will not be fixed
item.category: Advisories — CISA ICSA-26-286-01 (Inductive Automation Ignition), ICSA-26-288-01 (Eclipse Milo OPC UA), ICSA-26-279-01 (Johnson Controls EasyIO FG)
item.description: On 13 October CISA published ICSA-26-286-01 for Inductive Automation’s Ignition SCADA/HMI platform: CVE-2026-92817 (CVSS v3.1 8.8, v4.0 8.7) is an incorrect-authorization flaw that allows privilege escalation in versions 8.1.0–8.1.54 and 8.3.0–8.3.8, fixed in 8.1.55 and 8.3.9. On 15 October ICSA-26-288-01 covered six flaws in Eclipse Milo, the open-source Java OPC UA client and server library, the worst a missing-authorization bug at CVSS v3.1 8.2; version 1.1.5 fixes them and the 0.6.x line will not be fixed. Exposure depends on which OT products embed Milo, so expect follow-on vendor notices. On 6 October CISA republished Johnson Controls’ notice for EasyIO FG controller firmware: hard-coded credentials and improper privilege management (CVE-2026-27872 and CVE-2026-27873, CVSS 7.7 each), which CISA says are not remotely exploitable. The product is end-of-life with no fix, and the vendor recommends moving to EasyIO Neo R1. CISA lists critical manufacturing among the sectors for all three and knows of no public exploitation. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-286-01 (13 Oct 2026), ICSA-26-288-01 (15 Oct 2026) and ICSA-26-279-01 (6 Oct 2026) (primary) - Published 6–15 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] WAGO fixes a CVSS 9.8 BACnet flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker overwrite files on its controllers, as CODESYS patches its runtime and gateway
item.category: Vulnerability — WAGO BACnet/IP stack, CVSS 9.8; CODESYS runtime and gateway fixes (CERT@VDE)
item.description: CERT@VDE published WAGO advisory VDE-2025-102 on 1 October for CVE-2025-41753 (CVSS 9.8), a path traversal in the BACnet/IP stack: because BACnet File Object names are not properly validated, an unauthenticated remote attacker can read or overwrite arbitrary files on the device, which WAGO says may lead to full system compromise. Affected are the 750-811x, 750-821x, 751-9x01, 752-8303 and 762 series on wago_os_linux below 4.8.9; the fix is firmware 4.8.9 (FW30). The same day WAGO published VDE-2025-081 for CODESYS Control flaws in the same device families (CVE-2025-41738, CVSS 8.3, plus two lower-rated bugs) that can cause denial of service or run code when a user opens a malicious CODESYS project file; the fix is firmware 4.10.0 (FW32). On 30 September CODESYS itself disclosed CVE-2026-79625 (CVSS 8.1), a race condition that lets an authenticated user with monitoring access cause incorrect data processing, malfunction or denial of service in the Control runtime, and CVE-2026-76992 (CVSS 7.5), which can exhaust memory in a CODESYS client that connects to an attacker-controlled gateway. Both are fixed in 3.5.22.40, with Linux, ARM and other platform variants due in 4.23.0.0 in Q4 2026. No exploitation is reported for any of them. Because the CODESYS runtime is licensed to other controller makers, watch for their follow-on advisories (editorial note). - CERT@VDE VDE-2025-102 and VDE-2025-081 (WAGO), 1 Oct 2026; VDE-2026-097 and VDE-2026-094 (CODESYS), 30 Sep 2026 (primary) - Published 30 Sep–1 Oct 2026; CODESYS 4.23.0.0 expected Q4 2026

item.title: [Medium] ABB flags an AC500 V3 visualization denial-of-service, an Automation Builder project-file flaw and an unpatched Mint Workbench I bug
item.category: Vendor advisories — ABB AC500 V3, Automation Builder, Mint Workbench I
item.description: ABB published two notifications on 28 September, for its AC500 V3 PLCs and the Automation Builder engineering suite. In AC500 V3, invalid type usage in the visualization component could let an attacker cause a denial of service (3ADR011565). In Automation Builder, deserialization of untrusted data means a crafted project file or project archive could execute arbitrary code (3ADR011566). On 29 September ABB revised its Mint Workbench I advisory (first issued 17 September) for CVE-2026-19438 (CVSS v3.1 7.5, v4 8.2), a path traversal that lets a local attacker who already has file-write access read arbitrary system files; version 5876 and earlier are affected. There is no patch: the product reaches end of life at the end of 2026 (2027 in China), and ABB’s workarounds are to disable the MWI http service when it is not in use, restrict physical access and keep User Account Control on. No exploitation is reported. The Automation Builder flaw is the one to watch on engineering workstations, since project files routinely move between integrators, machine builders and plant staff. - ABB cyber security notifications 3ADR011565 and 3ADR011566, 28 Sep 2026; Mint Workbench I advisory (CVE-2026-19438) revision D, 29 Sep 2026 (primary) - Published 28–29 Sep 2026; Mint Workbench I end of life end-2026

item.title: [Medium] Murrelektronik says remove its AAS edge client: a CVSS 9.8 missing-authentication flaw lets anyone rewrite device data, and no fix is coming
item.category: Vulnerability — Murrelektronik AAS edge client, CVSS 9.8, no fix
item.description: CERT@VDE published Murrelektronik advisory VDE-2026-108 on 6 October for CVE-2026-94293 (CVSS 9.8), missing authentication in every version of the aas-edge-client reference implementation. An unauthenticated attacker can read and modify the Asset Administration Shell submodel data held on the edge device, and because changes are stored locally and forwarded to the central AAS server, connected systems may receive manipulated device information. There is no fix: Murrelektronik says the software was a reference implementation built for a trade-fair demonstrator and is no longer maintained, has archived its repositories and made them private, and tells users to stop using it and remove existing deployments. The Asset Administration Shell is an Industry 4.0 digital-twin standard, so the practical risk is reference code that was copied into a pilot or production data pipeline (editorial assessment). - CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-108 (Murrelektronik), 6 Oct 2026 (primary) - Published 6 Oct 2026; no fix planned

item.title: [Medium] CISA and the FBI tell operators to rein in third-party ICS integrators after a 2025 integrator breach exposed customer SCADA files
item.category: Guidance — Third-party ICS integrators; NIST OT security guide draft
item.description: CISA and the FBI published joint guidance on 24 September for critical infrastructure operators working with third-party ICS integrators. It draws on a March–April 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation company in which a foreign actor searched for “customers” and “SCADA” and staged about 800 files of customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics in nine archives. The agencies urge contract security requirements, least privilege, monitored and on-demand remote access, a full inventory of integrator-supplied equipment, offline backups and the ability to operate manually if the integrator is compromised. The victim’s named customers were power and transportation entities, not manufacturers, but plants routinely give OEMs, machine builders and integrators standing access to PLCs, robots and MES interfaces. Separately, NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Rev. 4, its OT security guide, on 21 September, restructured around CSF 2.0; comments are due 30 November. - CISA/FBI joint guidance, 24 Sep 2026 (per Industrial Cyber); NIST SP 800-82r4 draft, 21 Sep 2026 - Cites a Mar–Apr 2025 integrator compromise; SP 800-82r4 comments due 30 Nov 2026

item.title: [Medium] CISA’s final CIRCIA incident-reporting rule has reached White House review; who it covers will not be known until it is published
item.category: Regulation — CIRCIA final rule under White House review; text not yet public
item.description: The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged CISA’s final rule under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act (RIN 1670-AA04) for review on 1 October. The law sets 72-hour reporting for covered cyber incidents and 24-hour reporting for ransom payments by covered entities in critical-infrastructure sectors, which include critical manufacturing, but those duties start only on dates the final rule sets, and the text, including which entities are covered, is not public. The statutory deadline passed in October 2025 and CISA’s later targets of May and September 2026 slipped; HIPAA Journal reports publication is expected before year-end. In a report released 28 September from a July roundtable, GAO found that industry participants flagged the forthcoming CIRCIA rule and the SEC’s disclosure requirement as problems, citing differing thresholds, timelines and definitions. OIRA review is procedural, and the text can still change. - OIRA EO 12866 review record, received 1 Oct 2026 (primary); HIPAA Journal, 5 Oct 2026; GAO-26-109197 via Cybersecurity Dive, 29 Sep 2026 - Under review since 1 Oct 2026; no effective date yet
